content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-physics-speed","title":"Speed = Distance/Time","quick":"Speed tells how much distance is covered in one unit of time. Formula: Speed = Distance ÷ Time. Units must match, like km and hours.","full":"Speed shows how fast something moves. Think of an auto going from home to the kirana shop 10 km away in 2 hours. To find its speed, divide distance by time: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 km per hour. This means every hour the auto covers 5 km. Step by step: first note the total distance travelled, then note the total time taken, then divide distance by time. Speed and velocity look similar, but speed only tells how fast, while velocity also tells direction. For class 5, we only deal with speed, not direction.","traps":["Forgetting to divide and just writing the distance as the answer","Mixing up units, like using minutes when the question gives hours","Writing the answer without km/h or proper unit"],"misconception":"Child thinks speed is the total distance, not distance divided by time.","parent_questions":[{"q":"What do we do with the distance and time to find speed?","expected_answer_hint":"Divide distance by time."},{"q":"If a cycle covers 20 km in 4 hours, what is its speed?","expected_answer_hint":"20 ÷ 4 = 5 km/h."}],"check_question":{"q":"A bus travels 150 km in 3 hours.
